name: Vectrex
description: A 1982 home console with its own built-in 9-inch vector CRT, drawing sharp lines instead of pixels like arcade games such as Asteroids. It used plastic screen overlays to add colour and shipped with the game Mine Storm built in.
curiosities: Every Vectrex has the game Mine Storm built into its ROM.
Optional accessories included a light pen and the 3D Imager, a spinning-disc headset that produced colour 3D.
Milton Bradley bought GCE in 1983, and the console was discontinued after the 1983–84 market crash.
The rights holder later allowed non-commercial distribution of the Vectrex games, helping a homebrew scene that is still active.
story: Smith Engineering and General Consumer Electronics built the Vectrex in 1982, the only home console with its own vector screen, drawing lines like the Asteroids arcade machine.
Coloured plastic overlays added colour, and it had a light pen and 3D glasses.
The crash of 1983 ended it in 1984, but its makers later freed its games for anyone to share, and homebrew continues.
